summary.text: Climate change mitigation, also called decarbonisation, is action to limit the greenhouse gases in the atmosphere that cause climate change.
Its main actions are conserving energy and replacing fossil fuels with clean energy, with land-use changes and removing CO₂ from the air as secondary strategies.
Policies adopted so far are insufficient and would still lead to about 2.7 °C of warming by 2100, well above the Paris goal of below 2 °C.

facts.label: Land use share
facts.value: About a quarter of climate change

items.prompt: A country gets most of its power from solar and wind. On a calm, cloudy evening, what helps keep its electricity supply steady?

options.label: Adding more panels in the same town
Switching off the grid until morning
Lowering the voltage on every line

items.explain: Energy storage can even out power output, and grouping distant sources through long-distance transmission also helps.

items.prompt: A city plans to cut emissions by running everything on clean electricity. Which activity will be hardest to switch over?
items.explain: Clean electricity can usually replace fossil fuels for transport and heating, but cement production is among the harder processes to decarbonise.

items.prompt: A government sets a ceiling on total emissions and lets companies buy and sell permits to emit. What kind of policy is this?
items.explain: Carbon pricing systems either tax CO₂ emissions or cap total emissions and trade emission credits.

items.prompt: Human emissions have raised the amount of CO₂ in the air compared with pre-industrial times. By roughly how much?
items.explain: Human-caused emissions have increased atmospheric carbon dioxide by about 50% over pre-industrial levels.

items.prompt: An abandoned field regrows into forest entirely on its own and absorbs CO₂. Under the IPCC definition, does this count as carbon dioxide removal?

options.label: Yes, any CO₂ taken from the air counts
Yes, but only if the wood is buried
No, forests release more than they store

items.explain: The IPCC counts only human activities that remove and store CO₂, and excludes natural uptake not directly caused by people.

items.prompt: Clearing a forest and burning coal both release CO₂. What sets the coal's CO₂ apart?

options.label: It was buried underground in the slow carbon cycle
It is a short-lived gas that fades within years
It comes from the fast cycle of living plants
It is mostly methane rather than carbon dioxide

items.explain: Land use changes belong to the fast carbon cycle, while fossil fuels release CO₂ that was buried underground as part of the slow carbon cycle.
